subject: forestSpirit
reasoning:
I'm designing a kodama-like forest spirit: a tall mossy robed body, antler-branch head, a glowing-eyed mask face, leaf cape, shoulder mushrooms, and root-like feet with twig fingers, planning it as a single TypeScript module.

Building skeleton joints and chains...

Defining leg chains next, with hip-knee-ankle bones sized to reach the foot targets, then sweeping brown limb geometry and adding wedge-shaped feet. Settling on a side convention where +X is the left side for naming joints, then moving on to set up shoulder positions for the arms.

Now working out elbow and hand placement so distances stay within bone reach, adjusting hand targets slightly to fit, then building the shoulder-elbow-wrist chain parented to the spine with tapered limb sweeps. Adding twig-like fingers as a small radial ring of spikes on the wrist joint, angled outward and tilted toward the bone direction, before moving to shape a large rounded head using a scaled sphere.

Thinking through the hood geometry now, trying to size and position a mossy hemisphere shell so it sits behind the face without fully swallowing it, adjusting the sphere's angular range to form a back-covering cap.

For the eyes, I'm placing small dark scaled spheres embedded in the face surface with tiny glowing amber spheres layered on top for a lit effect, calculating the exact surface position using the face sphere's geometry so they sit flush rather than floating. For the mouth I'm planning a thin dark slit positioned along the lower jaw.

Now I'm working out the jaw as a small bone-colored half-sphere chin and adding a thin dark box for the mouth slit on the head. For the antlers, I'm sketching branching spike geometry using bezier paths that sweep upward and outward from the head, tapering the radius and placing smaller branch offshoots at points along each main spike's curve.

Adding leaf decals and spike branches...

Now I'm designing mushrooms for the shoulders and back using lathe geometry for the cap profile plus a stem, with the cap shaped as a closed loop of points and planning to add red coloring with white spot decals.

I'm also planning scattered leaf cards across the body and skirt surfaces as a cape-like effect, filtering placement by height, and considering a vine or rope sweep around the waist as a belt accent along the spine joints.

I decide to skip floating glow motes near the hand to keep things simple, and instead focus on the skirt's paint treatment—mottled moss tones possibly darkening toward the hem—plus a ring of small bark-colored spikes around the skirt's bottom edge to suggest a root fringe.

Now I'm working out the skirt's silhouette with a lathe profile that flares out and tapers down in blocky steps, making sure it overlaps the legs enough that only chunky root-like feet peek out below, complete with toe spikes and proper bounds checks so nothing clips below ground level.

I'm defining the color palette (bark, moss, pale cream, glow yellow, dark, red) and sketching the body sweep radius function so the torso tapers smoothly into the hips while keeping the shoulder joints positioned slightly outside the torso radius for a natural silhouette, then double-checking the neck-to-head and jaw joint placements for continuity. Writing SVG leaf code...

Now I'm setting up the scatter-and-cards system to place leaf cards across the body and skirt surfaces with varied size, lean, and bend, and detailing how the little mushroom props are built from a cylindrical stem and a latheed cap with painted spots. I'm finalizing these details before writing out the complete code.
